info.name: Ophir API
info.description:
REST API for a ride-hailing backend (Bun + Express + PostgreSQL + BullMQ + Valkey).

**Quick start**
1. Start Postgres + Valkey, `bun run migrate`, `bun run dev` **and** `bun run worker` (the worker does the matching).
2. Import this collection and the *Ophir - Local* environment.
3. Open **1. Happy path** and run it with the Collection Runner (or send each request top to bottom). It registers a rider and a driver, books, accepts, drives and completes a trip, and asserts along the way.
4. For the Admin folder run `bun run seed` once, then *Auth > Login admin*.

Tokens and ids are saved automatically in collection variables (riderToken, driverToken, rideId, offerId, ...).

item.name: 1. Happy path (run in order)
item.description: End-to-end trip. Use the Collection Runner on this folder. Needs the worker running.

request.description: Process is up.
Creates a rider and stores `riderToken`, `riderRefresh`, `riderId`, `riderEmail` as collection variables. Auth endpoints are rate-limited (20/min/IP by default).

exec: // Fresh random test area per run (>5 km from any driver left online by earlier runs, so offers always go to *this* run's driver).
set('dropLat', lat + 0.0448); set('dropLng', lng + 0.0125);   // ~5.5 km away
set('driverLat', lat + 0.0001); set('driverLng', lng + 0.0001); // ~15 m from pickup

request.description: Creates a driver account. Next: create the vehicle profile.
Required before going online. `vehicleType`: economy | comfort | xl.
Adds the driver to the Valkey geo index at this location (~20 m from the sample pickup).
Fare, ETA and nearby driver count per vehicle type.
Returns immediately; matching runs in the background worker. `409 ACTIVE_RIDE_EXISTS` if you already have a live ride (cancel or finish it first). `paymentMethod`: cash | card | wallet.

The BullMQ worker creates the offer asynchronously. In the Collection Runner this request retries itself up to 20 times (500 ms apart); when sending manually, just click Send again. **If it never finds an offer, the worker is not running.** Stores `offerId` and `rideId`.

exec: if (tries > 0) { const end = Date.now() + 500; while (Date.now() < end) {} }
pm.test("offer received for the requested ride", () => pm.expect(offers[0].ride.status).to.eql('searching'));
goto(pm.info.requestName); // in the Collection Runner this re-sends until the worker has created the offer
pm.test("offer arrived within ~10 s (is `bun run worker` running?)", () => pm.expect.fail("no offer"));

request.description: Atomic claim: only one driver can win a ride. 409 `OFFER_EXPIRED` if too slow (default 20 s).
Drivers ping every few seconds. Rate-limited to 20 per 10 s.
Driver must be within 0.5 km of pickup (409 `TOO_FAR_FROM_PICKUP` otherwise) — send a location update first.
Optional body: `{ "actualDistanceKm": 9.4, "actualDurationMin": 28 }`. Fare is never below the quote and capped at 3x.
1-5. Each party can rate once, on completed rides.

exec: pm.test('204, or 409 if already rated', () => pm.expect([204, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.description: Each logout is preceded by a fresh login. These invalidate the tokens other folders use, so run them last.
